narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Odysseus is absent while suitors eat his household's food and court Penelope, who has not agreed to marry one of them.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “Then the suitors came in and took their places on the benches and seats.3 Forthwith men servants poured water over their hands, maids went round with the bread-baskets, pages filled the mixing-bowls with wine and water, and they laid their hands upon the good things that were before them.”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: Homecoming matters because absence has already changed the home. The poem measures return not only in miles survived but in what remains to recover.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Read the household as part of the homecoming problem. The suitors’ behaviour shows what absence costs Penelope and Telemachus; the hero’s story is not confined to his own travels.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Carry this forward whenever Odysseus hides his name: identity and home are both being rebuilt.

quiz.prompt: What do the suitors do in Odysseus' hall?

choices.text: They guard the house from the Trojans
They sit down and eat the household's food

quiz.explanation: The passage describes the suitors taking their places and eating the household's food.

quiz.prompt: Why does Telemachus call the suitors a threat to his household?

choices.text: They are protecting the estate for Odysseus
They consume his property while pressuring his mother to marry
They have taken the household to Troy

quiz.explanation: Telemachus says the suitors eat up his house, press his mother, and make havoc of his estate.
